sections.title: Basic Concept of Direct and Indirect Speech
sections.content:
Direct Speech shows the exact words of the speaker inside quotation marks. Indirect Speech reports the same idea without quotation marks.

Step 1: Identify the reporting verb (said, says).
Step 2: Remove quotation marks and use 'that' if needed.
Step 3: Apply tense and pronoun changes if the reporting verb is in the past.

sections.title: Conversion of Assertive Sentences (Statements)
sections.content:
Assertive sentences are simple statements.

Rule:
1. Remove comma and quotation marks.
2. Add 'that' after the reporting verb.
3. Change tense if reporting verb is in the past.

Example:
Direct: He said, "She is happy."
Step 1: Remove quotation marks.
Step 2: Add 'that'.
Step 3: is → was (since 'said' is past).
Indirect: He said that she was happy.

sections.title: Changing Say/Says/Said to Tell/Tells/Told
sections.content:
When an object (me, him, her, us, them) is present, use tell instead of say.

Rule:
1. said to → told
2. says to → tells
3. say to → tell

Example:
Direct: He said to me, "You are late."
Step 1: said to → told
Step 2: are → were
Indirect: He told me that I was late.

sections.title: Basic Tense Shifts
sections.content:
If the reporting verb is in the past tense, the tense of the reported speech changes one step back.

Present Simple → Past Simple
Present Continuous → Past Continuous
Present Perfect → Past Perfect
Past Simple → Past Perfect

Example:
Direct: She said, "I play football."
Step 1: said (past)
Step 2: play → played
Indirect: She said that she played football.

sections.title: Pronoun Changes (SON Rule)
sections.content:
Use the SON rule for pronoun changes:
S = According to Subject
O = According to Object
N = No change (Universal truth)

Example:
Direct: He said to me, "I am your friend."
Step 1: I → he (Subject rule)
Step 2: your → my (Object rule)
Step 3: am → was
Indirect: He told me that he was my friend.

sections.title: Universal Truth (No Tense Change)
sections.content:
If the sentence expresses a universal truth or fact, the tense does not change.

Example:
Direct: The teacher said, "The sun rises in the east."
Step 1: It is a universal truth.
Step 2: Do not change tense.
Indirect: The teacher said that the sun rises in the east.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1. Forgetting to change 'said to' into 'told'.
2. Incorrect pronoun changes.
3. Changing tense in universal truths.
4. Forgetting to add 'that' in statements.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content:
1. Remove quotation marks.
2. Add 'that' (for statements).
3. Change said to → told (if object is present).
4. Shift tense one step back (if reporting verb is past).
5. Change pronouns using SON rule.

tricks.title: Remove Quotation Trick
tricks.explanation: Remove quotation marks and join the sentence with 'that'.
tricks.example: He said, "I am ready." → He said that he was ready.

tricks.title: Said to = Told Rule
tricks.explanation: If 'said to' is followed by an object, change it to 'told'.
tricks.example: She said to him → She told him.

tricks.title: One Step Back Rule
tricks.explanation: If reporting verb is past, shift the tense one step back.

tricks.title: I Change Trick
tricks.explanation: I changes according to the subject of reporting verb.
tricks.example: He said, "I am happy." → He said that he was happy.

tricks.title: You Change Trick
tricks.explanation: You changes according to the object.
tricks.example: He said to me, "You are smart." → He told me that I was smart.

tricks.title: Universal Truth Rule
tricks.explanation: Do not change tense if the sentence is a universal truth.
tricks.example: The teacher said that the earth moves around the sun.

tricks.title: Past to Past Perfect Rule
tricks.explanation: If both verbs are in past, change the reported verb into past perfect.
tricks.example: She said, "I finished." → She said that she had finished.

tricks.title: Object First Check
tricks.explanation: Always check if there is an object after the reporting verb.
tricks.example: He told her that she was right.

tricks.title: 3-Step Formula
tricks.explanation: 1. Check reporting verb 2. Change pronoun 3. Shift tense
tricks.example: He said to me, "I like you." → He told me that he liked me.
